html:
SMTO-DB-0002 — SMTO can't use the saved database connection it was given

GUID: 796601e4-d345-4e02-87d5-a3a78973fde5
Slug: database-context-invalid
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • SMTO was pointed at a saved entry that doesn't look like a complete database connection, or its saved link to that connection is out of date. No query was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store (where SMTO keeps saved connection details), select the database entry, open the Value tab and select Reveal & edit value. SMTO only treats an entry as a database connection when it includes the database's address, such as its host and database name.
  2. If the host, port or database name is missing, add it, then select Save. With these details filled in, SMTO can recognize the entry as a database it may connect to.
  3. In the conversation, type @ and pick that exact database entry from the list, then ask your question again. Picking the entry by name stops SMTO from using a similar entry or an older saved version of it.
  4. If this entry was edited after SMTO first used it in this conversation, tell SMTO that the connection changed and ask it to look up the entry again. SMTO refuses its older saved copy of a connection that has since been edited, so it needs to read the current one.

What success looks like

  • SMTO names the database connection you picked and answers your question about it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the name of the database entry. Don't paste passwords into the conversation or into the entry's name or description; keep them in the entry's own fields.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The database Skill rejected its saved context: the named Parameter Store entry is not a database_connection profile, the conversation's saved database setup has an invalid key, revision, identity or Gateway, or a discovery draft could not be committed.

What this means

  • Working-context validation rejects the saved profile shape/revision/public identity, profile resolution finds a non-database profile, or discovery cannot commit its selected profile. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • Working-context validation rejects the saved profile shape/revision/public identity, profile resolution finds a non-database profile, or discovery cannot commit its selected profile.

How to diagnose it

  • Separate malformed saved context from profile-type mismatch and discovery commit failure using the retained diagnostic.

How to fix it

  • Open the exact Parameter Store key and confirm its value has host/port/dbname-style fields (or database tags) so parameter_database_profile() returns profile_type database_connection. If the conversation's database working context is stale or malformed, let the agent rediscover the profile through the intended Gateway so a fresh setup (parameter_key, engine, identity, gateway, profile_revision) is validated. Keep credentials in the profile's own fields and never resubmit an old key or revision after the profile was edited.
  • Reopen the exact database profile and rediscover its working context through the intended Gateway. Keep credentials in the profile fields.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected profile and rediscovered public identity agree with the current revision.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
